question: Under para 1 of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers, a public officer shall not put himself in a position where:
options: His personal interest conflicts with his duties and responsibilities
His duties conflict with those of a superior officer
His salary exceeds the approved scale
His spouse holds a private business
explanation: Para 1 bars a conflict between personal interest and the duties and responsibilities of the office.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 1

question: Para 2 of the Code of Conduct provides that a public officer shall not receive:
options: Any allowance on top of his salary
Remuneration from more than one public office at the same time
A pension and a salary together
explanation: Without prejudice to para 1, an officer may not draw pay from more than one public office at once.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 2

question: Para 3 of the Code of Conduct prohibits certain senior officials, including the President, governors, ministers and legislators, from:
options: Holding more than one bank account in Nigeria
Holding or operating a bank account outside Nigeria
explanation: Para 3 covers the listed offices and bars foreign bank accounts.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 3

question: Para 4 of the Code of Conduct, on a retiree who receives a public pension, allows him to hold:
options: Any number of posts in government-owned companies
Only one remunerated post as chairman, director or employee of a government-owned company or public authority
No remunerated post of any kind
One post in a private company and one in a public company
explanation: While on a public pension, a retiree may hold only one remunerated post of the kind described.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 4

question: Para 5 of the Code of Conduct bars retired holders of which offices from working for foreign companies or enterprises?
options: Members of the National Assembly only
President, Vice-President, Chief Justice, governor and deputy governor
explanation: Para 5 names the President, Vice-President, Chief Justice, governor and deputy governor.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 5

question: Under para 6 of the Code of Conduct, a gift to a public officer from a company that has contracts with government is:
options: Always permitted if it is small
Presumed to be improper unless the contrary is proved
Permitted if declared at year end
Presumed proper unless the Bureau objects
explanation: Para 6 raises a presumption of impropriety for gifts from firms with government contracts.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 6

question: Under para 6 of the Code of Conduct, a gift given to a public officer on a public or ceremonial occasion is treated as:
options: A personal gift to the officer
A gift to the institution he represents
explanation: Gifts on public or ceremonial occasions are gifts to the institution the officer represents.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 6

question: Under para 7 of the Code of Conduct, listed senior officials may take loans only from:
options: Any person approved by the Head of Service
Government bodies or recognised financial institutions
explanation: Para 7 restricts loans to government bodies and recognised financial institutions, and bars benefits from companies, contractors or businessmen.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 7

question: Para 8 of the Code of Conduct makes it a breach to:
options: Attend a ceremony at government expense
Offer a public officer property, gifts or benefits as an inducement or bribe for a favour
explanation: Para 8 prohibits offering inducements or bribes to public officers.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 8

question: Para 9 of the Code of Conduct, on abuse of office, concerns an officer who:
options: Delegates a duty to a subordinate
Does an arbitrary act prejudicial to another person's rights, knowing it is unlawful or contrary to government policy
explanation: Para 9 covers arbitrary acts that harm another person's rights, done knowingly in abuse of office.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 9

question: Para 10 of the Code of Conduct bars a public officer from belonging to a society whose membership is:
options: Incompatible with the functions or dignity of his office
explanation: Para 10 prohibits membership of societies incompatible with the functions or dignity of the office.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 10

question: A public officer must declare his assets to the Code of Conduct Bureau within three months of taking office, and thereafter:
options: Only at the end of his term
At the end of every four years and at the end of his term
explanation: Para 11: within three months, then every four years, and at the end of the term of office.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 11

question: A public officer's asset declaration under para 11 must also cover the assets of:
explanation: The declaration covers the officer and his unmarried children under 18.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 11

question: Under para 11 of the Code of Conduct, an asset acquired after declaration that cannot be fairly attributed to approved income, gifts or loans is:
options: Presumed to be a breach unless the officer proves otherwise
Presumed lawful unless the Bureau disproves it
A matter for the police only
explanation: Para 11 puts the burden on the officer to explain unattributable assets.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 11

question: Under para 12 of the Code of Conduct, allegations that a public officer breached the Code must be made to:
options: The Head of the Civil Service
explanation: Para 12 requires such allegations to go to the Bureau, which may refer matters to the Tribunal.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 12

question: Under para 13 of the Code of Conduct, doing a prohibited act through a nominee, trustee or agent is:
options: Permitted if the agent is a relative
Itself a breach of the Code
Permitted if declared to the Bureau
explanation: Para 13 treats acts done through nominees, trustees or agents as breaches.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 13

question: The Code of Conduct Tribunal consists of:
options: A chairman and two other members
A chairman and four other members
A chairman and nine other members
explanation: Para 15 gives the Tribunal a chairman and two other members.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 15

question: The chairman of the Code of Conduct Tribunal must be qualified to be a judge of:
explanation: Para 15 requires qualification to be a judge of a superior court of record.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 15

question: Members of the Code of Conduct Tribunal are appointed by:
options: The President, on the recommendation of the National Judicial Council
The Chief Justice of Nigeria alone
explanation: Para 15: the President appoints on the National Judicial Council's recommendation.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 15

question: The chairman and members of the Code of Conduct Tribunal leave office at the age of:
explanation: Para 17 sets retirement at 70; those with at least ten years' service get a lifetime pension.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 17

question: Among the punishments the Code of Conduct Tribunal may impose on an officer found guilty is disqualification from public office for a period not exceeding:
explanation: Para 18(2) provides for disqualification for up to ten years.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 18(2)

question: Under para 18 of the Code of Conduct, property acquired through abuse or corruption of office may be:
options: Returned to the officer after ten years
Sold by the Bureau for its own use
Held in trust for the family
explanation: Para 18(2) provides for seizure and forfeiture to the State.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 18(2)

question: Appeals from decisions of the Code of Conduct Tribunal lie to:
options: The Court of Appeal, as of right
explanation: Para 18 gives an appeal as of right to the Court of Appeal.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 18

question: Regarding punishments imposed by the Code of Conduct Tribunal, the prerogative of mercy:
explanation: Para 18 says the prerogative of mercy does not apply to these punishments.
source: 1999 Constitution, Fifth Schedule, Part I, para 18

question: The Code of Conduct Bureau consists of:
options: A chairman and twelve other members
A chairman and nine other members
A chairman and two other members
explanation: Para 1 of Part I (Code of Conduct Bureau) gives ten members in all: a chairman and nine others.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 1

question: The minimum age of a member of the Code of Conduct Bureau at appointment is:
explanation: Members must be not less than fifty years old.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 1

question: A member of the Code of Conduct Bureau vacates office on attaining the age of:
explanation: Para 1 provides for vacation of office at seventy.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 1

question: The Code of Conduct Bureau may establish offices:
options: Only in the Federal Capital Territory
Only in the six geo-political zones
In each State of the Federation as needed
explanation: Para 2 permits offices in each State as necessary.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 2

question: Which function belongs to the Code of Conduct Bureau under para 3?
options: Receive and investigate complaints of breach and refer matters to the Tribunal where appropriate
explanation: The Bureau investigates and refers; the Tribunal adjudicates and punishes.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 3

question: Under para 3 of Part I (Code of Conduct Bureau), declarations of assets are kept by the Bureau and made available:
options: For inspection by any citizen of Nigeria, on terms set by the National Assembly
explanation: The Bureau keeps custody of declarations and makes them available for citizen inspection.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 3

question: The terms and conditions of service of staff of the Code of Conduct Bureau are the same as those of:
explanation: Para 4 aligns Bureau staff with civil servants of the Federation.
source: 1999 Constitution, Third Schedule, Part I, Code of Conduct Bureau, para 4

question: Under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, an official who fails without reasonable excuse to report a bribery offer or demand is liable to:
options: Imprisonment for up to five years
A fine of up to ₦100,000, or imprisonment for up to two years, or both
explanation: Duty to report: fine up to ₦100,000 or imprisonment up to two years, or both.
source: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, s.26 [as read via a summary of the placng text; spot-check]

question: Under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, bribery relating to public contracts and inflating prices above market rates attracts imprisonment for seven years or:
explanation: The penalty is seven years or a fine of one million naira.
source: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, s.25 [as read via a summary of the placng text; spot-check]

question: Under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, dealing with or concealing property that is the subject of specified offences attracts imprisonment for a term not exceeding:
explanation: Dealing with proceeds of the specified offences: up to five years.
source: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, s.27 [as read via a summary of the placng text; spot-check]

question: Under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, 'gratification' includes:
options: Forbearance from demanding money or money's worth due
Only offers made to public officers
explanation: Gratification covers money, gifts, offices, loan repayments, discounts, forbearance from demanding payment, protection from penalties and similar advantages.
source: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, s.2 [as read via a summary of the placng text; spot-check]

question: Which of the following is expressly covered by the Act's definition of 'gratification'?
options: A salary increase approved by the Federal Executive Council
explanation: The definition includes protection from penalties or proceedings, given or promised with intent to influence.
source: Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000, s.2 [as read via a summary of the placng text; spot-check]

question: Which body is established by s.4 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023?
options: The National Information Technology Development Agency
explanation: The Act establishes the Commission, replacing the National Data Protection Bureau as regulator.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.4

question: Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, a data controller of major importance must designate:
explanation: Section 32 requires a DPO with expert knowledge of data protection law.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.32

question: Under s.40 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, a controller must notify the Commission of a breach likely to risk individuals' rights within:
explanation: A processor tells the controller; the controller tells the Commission within 72 hours.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.40

question: Under s.40 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, where a breach poses a high risk to individuals, the controller must also:
options: Communicate it to the affected data subjects immediately
explanation: High-risk breaches must be communicated to affected data subjects immediately.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.40

question: Under s.26 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the silence or inactivity of a data subject:
explanation: Consent must be affirmative; silence or inactivity is not consent, and the controller bears the burden of proving it.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.26

question: Under s.31 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, before relying on consent to process a child's data, the controller must obtain consent of:
explanation: The section covers children and persons lacking legal capacity, and requires verification by appropriate means.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.31

question: Which of the following is sensitive personal data under s.30 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023?
explanation: Sensitive personal data includes genetic and biometric data, health status, religious beliefs and political opinions.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.30

question: Under s.44 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, controllers of major importance must register with the Commission within:
options: Six months of commencement or of becoming such a controller
explanation: Registration is within six months; significant changes are notified within 60 days.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.44

question: The maximum fine for a data controller or processor of major importance under s.48 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 is the greater of 2% of annual gross revenue in the preceding year and:
explanation: Higher tier: greater of ₦10m and 2% of prior-year gross revenue.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.48

question: The maximum fine for a data controller or processor not of major importance under s.48 is the greater of 2% of annual gross revenue in the preceding year and:
explanation: Standard tier: greater of ₦2m and 2% of prior-year gross revenue.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.48

question: Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the Chairman of the Governing Council of the Commission is:
options: A part-time chairman who is a retired judge, serving four years renewable once
explanation: Sections 8-10 provide a part-time Chairman, a retired judge, appointed by the President on the Minister's recommendation for four years, renewable once.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.8-10

question: The National Commissioner, chief executive of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, serves a term of:
explanation: Section 14: five years, renewable once; the role requires a data protection certification and at least ten years' senior experience.
source: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, s.14

question: The e-invoicing and electronic fiscal system announced by the Nigeria Revenue Service in February 2026 is also called:
explanation: The NRS notice described the E-Invoicing and Electronic Fiscal System, the Merchant Buyer Solution.
source: Nairametrics, 17 Feb 2026 [secondary source]

question: In the NRS e-invoicing roll-out, medium taxpayers are those with annual turnover of:
explanation: Medium taxpayers fall between ₦1bn and ₦5bn; emerging taxpayers are below ₦1bn.
source: Nairametrics, 17 Feb 2026 [secondary source]
